learningObjective: Characterize the embedding lookup as a gather kernel and identify its memory access pattern.
stem: The input embedding layer takes an int64 index tensor [B, N] and gathers rows from a weight table [V, D] (vocabulary V, hidden dim D). Which characterization of this kernel is correct?

options.text: It is a random-access read of individual elements: for each output element out[b, n, d] the kernel reads a single scalar table[idx[b,n], d], so global memory transactions are uncoalesced by design and the kernel is latency-bound.

It is functionally equivalent to a GEMM between a one-hot [B, N, V] input and the [V, D] table; a good implementation actually forms this one-hot and calls a sparse-GEMM primitive, which is faster than a hand-written gather kernel.
It is a reduction kernel that sums the embedding rows selected by all B*N indices; the output is [D] per batch item, and the runtime is dominated by the reduction depth log2(B*N).

It is a gather kernel with irregular but coalesced-per-row access: each of the B*N indices induces one contiguous read of D floats from the [V, D] table. FLOPs are zero; runtime is bandwidth-bound on the D-element rows read from the embedding table.

explanation: Input embedding = weight[indices[b, n]] gives a [B, N, D] output. Each of the B*N indices induces one contiguous read of D floats from the corresponding row of weight[V, D]. Within a warp, threads collaboratively load a single row (or a subset of rows) with coalesced accesses per row, but the row selection across warps is irregular. Zero FLOPs; strictly bandwidth-bound on the D bytes per index. The output side is also a coalesced write of D elements per token.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: within a row, threads read contiguous D floats — coalesced. Only the choice of row is data-dependent.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: no framework materializes the one-hot; the gather primitive is far more efficient.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: embedding is a gather, not a reduction; the output has shape [B, N, D], not [D].
optionExplanations.D: Correct: gather with per-row coalesced access.

assumptions: Warps cooperatively load a row rather than each thread choosing a different row.
nonImplications: Does not imply the backward is also just a gather; it is a scatter-add / segment-sum on the weight gradient.
Does not imply that embedding lookup is always the bottleneck; on modern LLMs it is typically a small fraction of runtime.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses row selection irregularity with per-element uncoalesced access.

performanceClaim.scope: Embedding lookup as a bandwidth-bound gather kernel
